as_told.title: Rocket pioneers Tsiolkovsky and Oberth believed they were in touch with angelic beings

plain: The founders of the great space programmes all believed they were in touch with non-human beings: Jack Parsons, who founded the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the American rocket lab, Konstantin Tsiolkovsky in Russia, and Wernher von Braun in Germany. Michels says this on several episodes, once crediting the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. Another time he softens it to Parsons only "implying" such contact, and on a third he names the German rocket pioneer Hermann Oberth and says Tsiolkovsky thought the beings were angels, which would mean space flight began partly as a spiritual quest.
